history.summary: CONFIRMED: the temple of Mosta (Mostadevata), the local rain/water god of Pithoragarh, on a hilltop at Dhunga Bhool on Digtoli road ~6 km from town, near Pithoragarh Fort and Chandak peak. Folk tradition says the saint Mostamanav came from Nepal and built it, and that its architecture recalls (is 'a replica of' per local lore) Nepal's Pashupatinath. 'Mostamanu' means the pavilion (manu) of Mosta; locals regard Mosta as a rain-bringer, equipped in legend with 22 thunderbolts, aided by Goddess Kalika and his brother Asura; buffalo and goats are sacrificed (for the servants of the deity, not the deities themselves). The annual monsoon fair draws devotees, artisans and government stalls. CONFLICT (flag): some travel pages call it a Shiva temple, but the dedicated sources say Mosta is a local deity (sometimes linked with Shiva). COORDINATES APPROXIMATE (verify): 29.626, 80.19563 from mapcarta/OpenStreetMap, ~5.5 km north of town, consistent with '6 km from Pithoragarh near Chandak'.

name: Mostamanu Temple
town_description: Pithoragarh is a hill town in the Kumaon Himalayas (~1,645 m), district headquarters of Pithoragarh district and a historic town of the Chand kings with the Pithoragarh Fort. It is the gateway to the Kailash-Mansarovar and Himalayan trek routes of eastern Uttarakhand.

travel.road: ~6 km from Pithoragarh town at Dhunga Bhool on Digtoli road; motorable road reaches the temple premises

visitor_information.best_time: October-May; the monsoon fair (August-September) is the liveliest but travel is difficult in heavy rain/landslide season
